ledger.note: c. 424: the Baishui Qiang kingdom of Dengzhi. 'Dengzhi was first founded by Xiang Shuzhi' (Book of Zhou), undated; the first dated ruler is Xiang Qudan, c. 424-453, who 'sent horses to the Liu Song dynasty as tribute'. Confidence 1: 424 is the first dated mention, the page says only '5th century'.

'In 554, Xiang Yanheng lost power after his state was attacked by the Tuyuhun'; Yuwen Tai of the Western Wei 'sent troops to escort him back to his domain'; infobox 'Disestablished: c. 554'. Confidence 2: the page says the state 'would have likely ceased to exist around this time'.

wars.outcome: Xiang Yanheng lost power to the Tuyuhun; Western Wei troops escorted him back to his domain; the state probably ended soon after.
wars.note: The page also dates Xiang Lanti's accession 509 and Dengzhi's tribute and embassies to Liu Song, Southern Qi, Northern Wei and Liang (undated vassal relations).

certainty.note: A mountain kingdom described by one line of area; no frontier on any page.

sources.title: Dengzhi
sources.note: Whole state: infobox (5th century to c. 554), capital, area, ruler table, 554 Tuyuhun attack and Western Wei escort.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; group scope 'the Di and Qiang states' frontiers'. One page only (the Xiang Yanheng page failed, URL_NOT_FOUND). Dengzhi was between Chouchi and Dangchang. The 424 start is the first dated mention. Whether Dengzhi's land passed to Western Wei, the Tuyuhun or Northern Zhou is not on the page. Rulers with an undated end are omitted from the strip. Family steppe by analogy with tuyuhun (no Qiang family exists).
